221	def _validate_orchestrator(orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition) -> None:
222	    _validate_qualified_identifier(orchestrator.id, "orchestrator.id")
223	    _validate_non_empty_string(orchestrator.name, "orchestrator.name")
224	    if orchestrator.kind not in ORCHESTRATOR_KINDS:
225	        raise OrchestratorValidationError(f"orchestrator.kind must be one of {sorted(ORCHESTRATOR_KINDS)}")
226	    _validate_non_empty_string(orchestrator.version, "orchestrator.version")
227	    _validate_runtime(orchestrator.runtime)
228	
229	    input_names = _validate_unique_named(orchestrator.inputs, "input")
230	    output_names = _validate_unique_named(orchestrator.outputs, "output")
231	    placeholders = set(input_names) | set(output_names)
232	    placeholders.update({"out", "brief", "python_exec", "orchestrator_args", "verbose"})
233	
234	    for port in orchestrator.inputs:
235	        _validate_port(port)
236	        if port.placeholder:
237	            _validate_non_empty_identifier(port.placeholder, f"input {port.name!r}.placeholder")
238	            placeholders.add(port.placeholder)
239	    for output in orchestrator.outputs:
240	        _validate_output(output)
241	        if output.placeholder:
242	            _validate_non_empty_identifier(output.placeholder, f"output {output.name!r}.placeholder")
243	            placeholders.add(output.placeholder)
244	        if output.path_template:
245	            _validate_placeholders(output.path_template, placeholders, f"output {output.name!r}.path_template")
246	    for index, child_executor in enumerate(orchestrator.child_executors):
247	        _validate_qualified_identifier(child_executor, f"orchestrator.child_executors[{index}]")
248	    for index, child_orchestrator in enumerate(orchestrator.child_orchestrators):
249	        _validate_qualified_identifier(child_orchestrator, f"orchestrator.child_orchestrators[{index}]")
250	    _validate_cache(orchestrator.cache)
251	    _validate_isolation(orchestrator.isolation)
252	    if orchestrator.runtime.command is not None:
253	        _validate_command(orchestrator.runtime.command, placeholders)
254	
255	
256	def _validate_runtime(runtime: RuntimeSpec) -> None:
257	    if runtime.kind not in RUNTIME_KINDS:
258	        raise OrchestratorValidationError(f"runtime.kind must be one of {sorted(RUNTIME_KINDS)}")
259	    if runtime.kind == "python":
260	        _validate_non_empty_string(runtime.module, "runtime.module")
261	        _validate_non_empty_string(runtime.function, "runtime.function")
262	        if runtime.command is not None:
263	            raise OrchestratorValidationError("python runtime cannot include runtime.command")
264	    if runtime.kind == "command":
265	        if runtime.command is None:
266	            raise OrchestratorValidationError("command runtime requires runtime.command")
267	        if runtime.module is not None or runtime.function is not None:
268	            raise OrchestratorValidationError("command runtime cannot include runtime.module or runtime.function")
269	
270	
271	def _validate_port(port: Port) -> None:
272	    _validate_non_empty_identifier(port.name, "input.name")
273	    if port.required and port.default is not None:
274	        raise OrchestratorValidationError(f"input {port.name!r} cannot be both required and have a default")
275	
276	
277	def _validate_output(output: Output) -> None:
278	    _validate_non_empty_identifier(output.name, "output.name")
279	    if output.mode not in OUTPUT_MODES:
280	        raise OrchestratorValidationError(f"output {output.name!r}.mode must be one of ['create', 'create_or_replace', 'mutate']")
281	
282	
283	def _validate_cache(cache: CachePolicy) -> None:
284	    if cache.mode not in CACHE_MODES:
285	        raise OrchestratorValidationError("cache.mode must be one of ['always_run', 'none', 'sentinel']")
286	    if cache.always_run and cache.sentinels:
287	        raise OrchestratorValidationError("cache.always_run cannot be combined with cache.sentinels")
288	    if cache.mode == "none" and (cache.sentinels or cache.always_run or cache.per_brief):
289	        raise OrchestratorValidationError("cache.mode 'none' cannot include sentinels, always_run, or per_brief")
290	    if cache.mode == "always_run" and not cache.always_run:
291	        raise OrchestratorValidationError("cache.mode 'always_run' requires cache.always_run=true")
292	
293	
294	def _validate_isolation(isolation: IsolationMetadata) -> None:
295	    if isolation.mode not in ISOLATION_MODES:
296	        raise OrchestratorValidationError("isolation.mode must be one of ['in_process', 'subprocess']")
297	
298	
299	def _validate_command(command: CommandSpec, placeholders: set[str]) -> None:
300	    if not command.argv:
301	        raise OrchestratorValidationError("runtime.command.argv must contain at least one argument")
302	    for index, part in enumerate(command.argv):
303	        _validate_non_empty_string(part, f"runtime.command.argv[{index}]")
304	        _validate_placeholders(part, placeholders, f"runtime.command.argv[{index}]")
305	    if command.cwd:
306	        _validate_placeholders(command.cwd, placeholders, "runtime.command.cwd")
307	    for key, value in command.env.items():
308	        _validate_non_empty_string(key, "runtime.command.env key")
309	        _validate_placeholders(value, placeholders, f"runtime.command.env[{key!r}]")
310

312	def _validate_placeholders(value: str, allowed: set[str], path: str) -> None:
313	    for placeholder in re.findall(r"\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}", value):
314	        if placeholder not in allowed:
315	            raise OrchestratorValidationError(f"{path} uses unknown placeholder {{{placeholder}}}")
316

318	def _validate_unique_named(values: tuple[Port, ...] | tuple[Output, ...], label: str) -> set[str]:
319	    names: set[str] = set()
320	    for value in values:
321	        if value.name in names:
322	            raise OrchestratorValidationError(f"duplicate {label} name {value.name!r}")
323	        names.add(value.name)
324	    return names

132	def run_orchestrator(request: OrchestratorRunRequest, registry: OrchestratorRegistry | None = None) -> OrchestratorRunResult:
133	    active_registry = registry or load_default_registry()
134	    orchestrator = active_registry.get(request.orchestrator_id)
135	    project_context, effective_request = _prepare_project_request(request, orchestrator)
136	    context = None if project_context is not None else thread_wrapper.begin_orchestrator_run(effective_request, orchestrator)
137	    try:
138	        result = _run_orchestrator_inner(effective_request, orchestrator)
139	    except Exception as exc:
140	        thread_wrapper.finalize_exception(context, exc)
141	        if project_context is not None:
142	            _finalize_project_orchestrator(project_context, effective_request, status="error", returncode=-1, error=exc)
143	        raise
144	    thread_wrapper.finalize_result(context, result)
145	    if project_context is not None:
146	        _finalize_project_orchestrator(
147	            project_context,
148	            effective_request,
149	            status=_project_status_for_result(result),
150	            returncode=result.returncode,
151	        )
152	    return result

154	
155	def _run_orchestrator_inner(request: OrchestratorRunRequest, orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition) -> OrchestratorRunResult:
156	    values = _request_values(request)
157	    _validate_out_requirement(orchestrator, request)
158	    _validate_required_inputs(orchestrator, values)
159	    if orchestrator.runtime.kind == "python":
160	        return _ensure_dry_run_plan(_run_python_orchestrator(orchestrator, request))
161	    if orchestrator.runtime.kind == "command":
162	        return _ensure_dry_run_plan(_run_command_orchestrator(orchestrator, request, values))
163	    raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"unsupported orchestrator runtime kind {orchestrator.runtime.kind!r}")
164	
165	
166	def build_orchestrator_command(request: OrchestratorRunRequest, registry: OrchestratorRegistry | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
167	    active_registry = registry or load_default_registry()
168	    orchestrator = active_registry.get(request.orchestrator_id)
169	    values = _request_values(request)
170	    _validate_out_requirement(orchestrator, request)
171	    _validate_required_inputs(orchestrator, values)
172	    if orchestrator.runtime.kind != "command":
173	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} does not use a command runtime")
174	    command, _, _ = _expand_command_runtime(orchestrator, request, values)
175	    return command

178	def _run_python_orchestrator(orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition, request: OrchestratorRunRequest) -> OrchestratorRunResult:
179	    runtime = orchestrator.runtime
180	    if not runtime.module or not runtime.function:
181	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} has an invalid Python runtime")
182	    try:
183	        module = importlib.import_module(runtime.module)
184	    except Exception as exc:
185	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"failed to import orchestrator runtime module {runtime.module!r}: {exc}") from exc
186	    target = getattr(module, runtime.function, None)
187	    if not callable(target):
188	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"orchestrator runtime target {runtime.module}.{runtime.function} is not callable")
189	    try:
190	        raw_result = target(request, orchestrator)
191	    except OrchestratorRunnerError:
192	        raise
193	    except Exception as exc:
194	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} Python runtime failed: {exc}") from exc
195	    return _normalize_python_result(orchestrator, request, raw_result)
196	
197	
198	def _run_command_orchestrator(
199	    orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition,
200	    request: OrchestratorRunRequest,
201	    values: Mapping[str, Any],
202	) -> OrchestratorRunResult:
203	    command, cwd, env = _expand_command_runtime(orchestrator, request, values)
204	    if request.dry_run:
205	        planned_commands = (command,)
206	        return OrchestratorRunResult(
207	            orchestrator_id=orchestrator.id,
208	            kind=orchestrator.kind,
209	            runtime_kind="command",
210	            command=command,
211	            planned_commands=planned_commands,
212	            cwd=cwd,
213	            env=env,
214	            returncode=None,
215	            dry_run=True,
216	            plan=_plan_from_commands(planned_commands, prefix=orchestrator.id),
217	        )
218	    completed = subprocess.run(
219	        list(command),
220	        cwd=cwd,
221	        env={**os.environ, **env, **_project_subprocess_env(request), **thread_wrapper.subprocess_env()},
222	        check=False,
223	    )
224	    return OrchestratorRunResult(
225	        orchestrator_id=orchestrator.id,
226	        kind=orchestrator.kind,
227	        runtime_kind="command",
228	        command=command,
229	        planned_commands=(command,),
230	        cwd=cwd,
231	        env=env,
232	        returncode=completed.returncode,
233	    )
234	
235	
236	def _expand_command_runtime(
237	    orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition,
238	    request: OrchestratorRunRequest,
239	    values: Mapping[str, Any],
240	) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], str | None, dict[str, str]]:
241	    command_spec = orchestrator.runtime.command
242	    if command_spec is None:
243	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} has no command runtime")
244	    placeholders = _placeholder_values(orchestrator, request, values)
245	    argv: list[str] = []
246	    for part in command_spec.argv:
247	        if part == "{orchestrator_args}":
248	            argv.extend(request.orchestrator_args)
249	        else:
250	            argv.append(_expand_placeholders(part, placeholders))
251	    cwd = _expand_placeholders(command_spec.cwd, placeholders) if command_spec.cwd else None
252	    env = {[REDACTED](value, placeholders) for key, value in command_spec.env.items()}
253	    return tuple(argv), cwd, env

256	def _normalize_python_result(
257	    orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition,
258	    request: OrchestratorRunRequest,
259	    raw_result: Any,
260	) -> OrchestratorRunResult:
261	    if isinstance(raw_result, OrchestratorRunResult):
262	        return _ensure_dry_run_plan(raw_result)
263	    if raw_result is None:
264	        return _ensure_dry_run_plan(OrchestratorRunResult(
265	            orchestrator_id=orchestrator.id,
266	            kind=orchestrator.kind,
267	            runtime_kind="python",
268	            returncode=None if request.dry_run else 0,
269	            dry_run=request.dry_run,
270	        ))
271	    if isinstance(raw_result, int):
272	        return _ensure_dry_run_plan(OrchestratorRunResult(
273	            orchestrator_id=orchestrator.id,
274	            kind=orchestrator.kind,
275	            runtime_kind="python",
276	            returncode=None if request.dry_run else raw_result,
277	            dry_run=request.dry_run,
278	        ))
279	    if isinstance(raw_result, dict):
280	        return _result_from_mapping(orchestrator, request, raw_result)
281	    raise OrchestratorRunnerError(
282	        f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} returned unsupported result type {type(raw_result).__name__}; "
283	        "expected OrchestratorRunResult, dict, int, or None"
284	    )
285	
286	
287	def _result_from_mapping(
288	    orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition,
289	    request: OrchestratorRunRequest,
290	    raw: Mapping[str, Any],
291	) -> OrchestratorRunResult:
292	    command = _tuple_of_strings(raw.get("command", ()), "command")
293	    planned_commands = _planned_commands(raw.get("planned_commands", (command,) if command else ()))
294	    errors = tuple(
295	        error if isinstance(error, OrchestratorRunError) else OrchestratorRunError(str(error))
296	        for error in raw.get("errors", ())
297	    )
298	    returncode = raw.get("returncode")
299	    if request.dry_run and returncode is not None:
300	        returncode = None
301	    elif returncode is not None:
302	        returncode = int(returncode)
303	    plan = _plan_from_raw(raw.get("plan")) if "plan" in raw else None
304	    return _ensure_dry_run_plan(OrchestratorRunResult(
305	        orchestrator_id=str(raw.get("orchestrator_id") or orchestrator.id),
306	        kind=str(raw.get("kind") or orchestrator.kind),
307	        runtime_kind=str(raw.get("runtime_kind") or "python"),
308	        command=command,
309	        planned_commands=planned_commands,
310	        cwd=_optional_string(raw.get("cwd")),
311	        env={str(key): str(value) for key, value in dict(raw.get("env", {})).items()},
312	        returncode=returncode,
313	        dry_run=bool(raw.get("dry_run", request.dry_run)),
314	        outputs=dict(raw.get("outputs", {})),
315	        errors=errors,
316	        plan=plan,
317	    ))
318

320	def _ensure_dry_run_plan(result: OrchestratorRunResult) -> OrchestratorRunResult:
321	    if not result.dry_run or result.plan is not None:
322	        return result
323	    return replace(result, plan=_plan_from_commands(result.planned_commands, prefix=result.orchestrator_id))

326	def _plan_from_commands(commands: tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...], *, prefix: str) -> OrchestratorPlan:
327	    steps = tuple(
328	        OrchestratorPlanStep(
329	            id=f"{prefix}.step_{index + 1}",
330	            kind="command",
331	            command=command,
332	        )
333	        for index, command in enumerate(commands)
334	    )
335	    return OrchestratorPlan(steps=steps)

338	def _plan_from_raw(raw: Any) -> OrchestratorPlan | None:
339	    if raw is None:
340	        return None
341	    if isinstance(raw, OrchestratorPlan):
342	        return raw
343	    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
344	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError("plan must be an object")
345	    raw_steps = raw.get("steps", ())
346	    if not isinstance(raw_steps, (list, tuple)):
347	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError("plan.steps must be a list")
348	    return OrchestratorPlan(
349	        steps=tuple(_plan_step_from_raw(item, f"plan.steps[{index}]") for index, item in enumerate(raw_steps)),
350	        summary=str(raw.get("summary") or ""),
351	    )

354	def _plan_step_from_raw(raw: Any, path: str) -> OrchestratorPlanStep:
355	    if isinstance(raw, OrchestratorPlanStep):
356	        return raw
357	    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
358	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"{path} must be an object")
359	    step_id = raw.get("id")
360	    if not isinstance(step_id, str) or not step_id.strip():
361	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"{path}.id must be a non-empty string")
362	    return OrchestratorPlanStep(
363	        id=step_id,
364	        kind=str(raw.get("kind") or "command"),
365	        command=_tuple_of_strings(raw.get("command", ()), f"{path}.command"),
366	        description=str(raw.get("description") or ""),
367	        metadata=dict(raw.get("metadata", {})),
368	    )

371	def _placeholder_values(orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition, request: OrchestratorRunRequest, values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
372	    placeholders: dict[str, str] = {
373	        "python_exec": str(values.get("python_exec") or request.python_exec or sys.executable),
374	        "orchestrator_args": " ".join(request.orchestrator_args),
375	        "verbose": str(bool(values.get("verbose", request.verbose))).lower(),
376	    }
377	    if request.out is not None:
378	        placeholders["out"] = str(Path(request.out).expanduser().resolve())
379	    brief = values.get("brief") or request.brief
380	    if brief is not None:
381	        placeholders["brief"] = str(Path(str(brief)).expanduser().resolve())
382	    for key, value in values.items():
383	        if value is None:
384	            continue
385	        if key == "verbose":
386	            placeholders[key] = str(bool(value)).lower()
387	        else:
388	            placeholders[key] = _stringify_value(value)
389	    for output in orchestrator.outputs:
390	        output_path = _output_value(output, request, placeholders)
391	        placeholders[output.name] = output_path
392	        if output.placeholder:
393	            placeholders[output.placeholder] = output_path
394	    return placeholders

396	
397	def _prepare_project_request(
398	    request: OrchestratorRunRequest,
399	    orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition,
400	) -> tuple[ProjectRunContext | None, OrchestratorRunRequest]:
401	    if not request.project:
402	        return None, request
403	    reject_project_with_out(request.project, request.out)
404	    if orchestrator.runtime.kind != "command":
405	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError("--project is currently supported only for command-runtime orchestrators")
406	    if _orchestrator_requires_output_path(orchestrator) and _has_cli_option(tuple(request.orchestrator_args), "--out"):
407	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(
408	            f"--project cannot be combined with passthrough --out for {orchestrator.id}"
409	        )
410	    context = prepare_project_run(
411	        request.project,
412	        tool_id=orchestrator.id,
413	        kind="orchestrator",
414	        argv=_project_argv(request),
415	        metadata={"dry_run": bool(request.dry_run)},
416	    )
417	    args = tuple(request.orchestrator_args)
418	    if _orchestrator_requires_output_path(orchestrator):
419	        args = (*args, "--out", str(context.run_root))
420	    return context, replace(request, out=context.run_root, orchestrator_args=args)
421	
422	
423	def _orchestrator_requires_output_path(orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition) -> bool:
424	    return bool(orchestrator.metadata.get("requires_output_path"))
425	
426	
427	def _project_argv(request: OrchestratorRunRequest) -> list[str]:
428	    argv = ["orchestrators", "run", request.orchestrator_id]
429	    if request.project:
430	        argv.extend(["--project", request.project])
431	    if request.brief:
432	        argv.extend(["--brief", str(request.brief)])
433	    for key, value in request.inputs.items():
434	        argv.extend(["--input", f"{key}={_stringify_value(value)}"])
435	    if request.dry_run:
436	        argv.append("--dry-run")
437	    if request.python_exec:
438	        argv.extend(["--python-exec", request.python_exec])
439	    if request.verbose:
440	        argv.append("--verbose")
441	    if request.orchestrator_args:
442	        argv.append("--")
443	        argv.extend(request.orchestrator_args)
444	    return argv

447	def _project_status_for_result(result: OrchestratorRunResult) -> str:
448	    if result.dry_run:
449	        return "skipped"
450	    if not result.ok:
451	        return "failed"
452	    return "success"

455	def _finalize_project_orchestrator(
456	    context: ProjectRunContext,
457	    request: OrchestratorRunRequest,
458	    *,
459	    status: str,
460	    returncode: int | None,
461	    error: BaseException | str | None = None,
462	) -> None:
463	    metadata = {"dry_run": bool(request.dry_run)}
464	    finalize_project_run(

469	        metadata=metadata,

474	def _project_subprocess_env(request: OrchestratorRunRequest) -> dict[str, str]:
475	    return project_thread_env() if request.project else {}

477	
478	def _has_cli_option(args: tuple[str, ...], option: str) -> bool:
479	    return any(arg == option or arg.startswith(f"{option}=") for arg in args)
480	
481	
482	def _output_value(output: Output, request: OrchestratorRunRequest, placeholders: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
483	    if output.name in request.outputs:
484	        return _stringify_value(request.outputs[output.name])
485	    if output.placeholder and output.placeholder in request.outputs:
486	        return _stringify_value(request.outputs[output.placeholder])
487	    if output.path_template:
488	        return _expand_placeholders(output.path_template, placeholders)
489	    if request.out is None:
490	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"--out is required to derive output {output.name!r}")
491	    return str((Path(request.out).expanduser().resolve() / output.name).resolve())
492	
493	
494	def _expand_placeholders(value: str, placeholders: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
495	    def replace(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
496	        key = match.group(1)
497	        if key not in placeholders:
498	            raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"missing value for placeholder {{{key}}}")
499	        return placeholders[key]
500	
501	    return _PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(replace, value)
502	
503	
504	def _validate_required_inputs(orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition, values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
505	    missing = [
506	        port.name
507	        for port in orchestrator.inputs
508	        if port.required and port.default is None and not _has_value(values.get(port.name))
509	    ]
510	    if missing:
511	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"orchestrator {orchestrator.id!r} missing required input(s): {', '.join(missing)}")
512	
513	
514	def _validate_out_requirement(orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition, request: OrchestratorRunRequest) -> None:
515	    if request.out is not None:
516	        return
517	    if _orchestrator_requires_output_path(orchestrator):
518	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"--out is required for {orchestrator.id}")
519	    if request.dry_run:
520	        return
521	    if orchestrator.runtime.kind == "command" and _command_runtime_requires_out(orchestrator, request):
522	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError("--out is required for command runtime placeholders")
523	    raise OrchestratorRunnerError("--out is required for orchestrator execution")
524	
525	
526	def _command_runtime_requires_out(orchestrator: OrchestratorDefinition, request: OrchestratorRunRequest) -> bool:
527	    command = orchestrator.runtime.command
528	    if command is None:
529	        return False
530	    values = [*command.argv]
531	    if command.cwd:
532	        values.append(command.cwd)
533	    values.extend(command.env.values())
534	    if any(_uses_placeholder(value, "out") for value in values):
535	        return True
536	    for output in orchestrator.outputs:
537	        if output.name in request.outputs or (output.placeholder and output.placeholder in request.outputs):
538	            continue
539	        if output.path_template is None or _uses_placeholder(output.path_template, "out"):
540	            return True
541	    return False
542	
543	
544	def _uses_placeholder(value: str, placeholder: str) -> bool:
545	    return placeholder in _PLACEHOLDER_RE.findall(value)
546	
547	
548	def _request_values(request: OrchestratorRunRequest) -> dict[str, Any]:
549	    values = dict(request.inputs)
550	    if request.brief is not None and "brief" not in values:
551	        values["brief"] = request.brief
552	    if request.python_exec is not None and "python_exec" not in values:
553	        values["python_exec"] = request.python_exec
554	    values.setdefault("verbose", request.verbose)
555	    return values
556	
557	
558	def _planned_commands(raw: Any) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], ...]:
559	    if raw is None:
560	        return ()
561	    if not isinstance(raw, (list, tuple)):
562	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError("planned_commands must be a list of command lists")
563	    commands: list[tuple[str, ...]] = []
564	    for index, item in enumerate(raw):
565	        commands.append(_tuple_of_strings(item, f"planned_commands[{index}]"))
566	    return tuple(commands)
567	
568	
569	def _tuple_of_strings(raw: Any, path: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
570	    if raw is None or raw == ():
571	        return ()
572	    if not isinstance(raw, (list, tuple)):
573	        raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"{path} must be a list")
574	    result: list[str] = []
575	    for index, item in enumerate(raw):
576	        if not isinstance(item, str):
577	            raise OrchestratorRunnerError(f"{path}[{index}] must be a string")
578	        result.append(item)
579	    return tuple(result)
580	
581	
582	def _optional_string(value: Any) -> str | None:
583	    if value is None:
584	        return None
585	    return str(value)

> AGENT

Short answer: **no, not first-class.** The orchestrator schema only knows two `runtime.kind` values — `python` and `command` — and `runner.py` will reject anything else (`artagents/core/orchestrator/schema.py:24`, `artagents/core/orchestrator/runner.py:163`). Every step is something the executor actually runs.

There are two adjacent things that hint at it but don't deliver it:

- `OrchestratorPlanStep.kind` (`artagents/core/orchestrator/runner.py:64`) is a free-form string defaulting to `"command"`. The runner only emits `kind="command"` itself, but a Python orchestrator returning a dict could populate a plan with steps of any kind — including `"manual"` — and they'd survive serialization. Nothing consumes that today (no pause, no checkbox UI), so it's just metadata.
- `packs/builtin/open_in_reigh` and `packs/builtin/human_notes` show the current pattern for human-in-the-loop: implement it as a regular code step that prints handoff instructions or ingests notes the human produced offline. The "manual" part lives outside the orchestrator.

If you want a real mixed checklist (some steps execute, some say "go do X and confirm"), the cleanest hook points are:

1. Extend `RUNTIME_KINDS`/`OrchestratorPlanStep` with a `manual` kind that carries a description + acknowledgement file path, and have the runner treat it as a pause-and-record step.
2. Or, until that exists, model it as a Python orchestrator that emits an `OrchestratorPlan` with `kind="manual"` steps and writes a checklist file into `out/` for the human to tick off — fully convention-based, no schema change.

> AGENT

Honest answer: today ArtAgents gives you **after-the-fact audit**, not **live on-task enforcement**.

What you actually get right now:

- **Per-step provenance.** Every executor/orchestrator run is wrapped by `thread_wrapper.begin_orchestrator_run` (`artagents/core/orchestrator/runner.py:136`) and finalized either with a result or an exception. Each call lands in the thread index with inputs, outputs, returncode.
- **Project-run isolation.** `prepare_project_run` / `finalize_project_run` (`artagents/core/project/run.py`) give every invocation its own immutable directory + `run.json` with status (`success`/`failed`/`skipped`/`error`) and the full argv. So you can always reconstruct what an agent did and in what order.
- **Schema gates on code steps.** Required inputs are enforced (`_validate_required_inputs`, `runner.py:504`), and `CachePolicy.sentinels` lets a step refuse to run until a prior artifact exists. That's the closest thing to a process-order check today.

What is **not** there:

- No "task mode" / state machine. Nothing says "orchestrator X is in flight and step 3 is next" — runs are independent invocations from the runner's POV.
- No human-ack primitive. A manual step has no way to block the runner until a person signs off.
- No skip-detection. An agent can run step 5 before step 2 and the runner won't notice; only the audit log will reveal it later.

If you want real "keep the agent in check," the smallest set of additions that play nicely with what's there:

1. **Manual step kind** — extend `RUNTIME_KINDS` (or just `OrchestratorPlanStep.kind`) with `manual`. The runner writes `<run>/steps/<id>.pending.json` and refuses to start the next step until it's replaced by `<id>.done.json`. Acknowledgement comes from a new CLI verb (`artagents orchestrators ack <run-id> <step-id>`) that records who/when, signed into the project run record.
2. **Declarative process tape.** Have orchestrators publish their step list at start of run, materialize it as a checklist file in the run dir, and make the runner the only writer. Out-of-order or skipped steps = error. This piggybacks on the existing `OrchestratorPlan` shape — it just isn't authoritative today.
3. **Use `cache.sentinels` as a sequencing primitive.** Each step declares the sentinel artifact from the previous step it depends on; the existing validator (`_validate_cache`, `schema.py:283`) already understands it. Turns "did the human do step 2" into "does `step_2.done.json` exist."

Combined: provenance you already have + an ack file + sentinel ordering = a checklist the agent can't fast-forward through. Want me to draft (1) as a concrete patch to `schema.py` + `runner.py`?

> DEVELOPER

So how would they enter task mode? How would you nudge them forawrds executing everything?

> AGENT

There's a key design choice baked into ArtAgents that shapes the answer: the runner is a CLI, not a daemon. Nothing in the repo runs continuously to push the agent — invocations are pulled by whoever is at the keyboard (human, Claude Code, Lota). So "nudging" has to be either (a) a refuse-non-canonical gate that makes the *next legal step* the only thing that works, or (b) a harness-level hook outside ArtAgents that re-invokes the agent. You almost certainly want both.

**Entering task mode = explicit handshake.** A new verb, e.g.:

```
artagents orchestrators start <orchestrator-id> --project foo
```

does three things, all file-based so it survives process death:

1. Calls `prepare_project_run` and materializes the orchestrator's full step list into `runs/<id>/checklist.json` with a `cursor: 0`. This is the process tape.
2. Writes `runs/<id>/AGENT.md` — a short contract: "you are running X. The next step is Y. To advance: `artagents next`. To ack a manual step: `artagents ack <step-id>`. Do not invoke other orchestrators against this project until this run is `done` or `aborted`." The agent reads this once and pins it in context.
3. Sets `@active` to the new run id (you already have `@active` in `threads/`). That's the "I'm in task mode" flag — there's an in-flight project run and the gate is armed.

**The nudge — three layered mechanisms:**

1. **`artagents next` (single verb the agent memorizes).** Reads `@active`, opens `checklist.json`, prints the next step. For a code step it prints the exact `artagents orchestrators run …` command (copy-pasteable). For a manual step it prints the instruction and the ack command. This is the *forward pull*: the agent never has to figure out what's next, only run `next`.

2. **Refuse-non-canonical at the gate.** In `runner.py`, before `_run_orchestrator_inner`, check: is there an in-flight run for this project, and does this invocation match `checklist[cursor]`? If not, error: `not the next step — current cursor is 3 (transcribe); run \`artagents next\``. This is what keeps the agent honest. Out-of-order is rejected, skipping is rejected, re-running is rejected unless the step's cache policy allows it. The agent can't drift because the only thing the system will accept is the next legal move.

3. **Auto-advance on success.** When a code step finishes with `ok=True`, `finalize_project_run` bumps the cursor and prints the next step in the result (`next: artagents orchestrators run …`). For a manual step, `ack` does the same. Every successful action ends with the next instruction stapled to its output, so the agent never goes silent between steps.

**Where the harness comes in.** Inside Claude Code specifically, the strongest active push is a `Stop` hook in `settings.json` that runs `artagents next` and injects the output into the next turn. That makes ArtAgents *literally* nudge the agent on every idle moment: even if the agent stops mid-checklist, the harness re-prompts it with "next step: X." That's outside ArtAgents itself — it's a `update-config` move — but it's the piece that turns "system refuses bad moves" into "system continuously surfaces the right one." Outside Claude Code, the equivalent is a shell prompt that runs `artagents next` whenever you `cd` into the project, or a Lota loop that polls.

**Failsafes worth adding while you're in there:**

- **Heartbeat / stall detection.** `next` and `ack` touch `runs/<id>/heartbeat.json`. `artagents doctor` flags any run idle past N minutes as `stalled`. Soft signal for the operator, not a block.
- **Manual ack must carry evidence.** `ack` takes a `--evidence` (a path, a git SHA, a one-line note). It's stored in the step record. Without evidence the run records `acked_blind: true` so audit shows where the human waved it through.
- **Abort, not skip.** No `skip` verb. If a step genuinely can't run, `abort` ends the run with a reason; the agent has to `start` a new one. Skipping silently is the failure mode you're trying to prevent.

Net shape: **start** arms the gate, **next** tells the agent what to do, the **runner refuses** anything else, **ack/auto-advance** moves the cursor, and a **Stop hook** turns the whole thing into something that pushes back when the agent goes quiet. None of it requires a daemon, all of it is files in `runs/<id>/`, and the existing thread/project-run plumbing already does ~70% of the work.

> DEVELOPER

And how should the 'task' list be stored?

> AGENT

Two files per run, append-only event log, and a project-level pointer. Five-ish artifacts, none of them clever:

```
projects/<slug>/
  active_run.json                  # {"run_id":"01HXX..."} or absent — the "task mode" flag
  runs/<run-id>/
    run.json                       # already exists (project-run record)
    checklist.json                 # immutable plan, written once at `start`
    cursor.json                    # mutable head: where we are, status
    events.jsonl                   # append-only audit, source of truth
    heartbeat.json                 # touched by next/ack
    steps/<step-id>/               # per-step artifacts + evidence
```

**`checklist.json` — frozen contract.** Written once at `start`, never mutated. If you need to change it, you `abort` and `start` a new run. This is the single thing that prevents the agent from rewriting its own marching orders mid-task.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "run_id": "01HXX...",
  "orchestrator_id": "hype.cut",
  "steps": [
    {"id":"transcribe","kind":"code",
     "command":["artagents","executors","run","hype.transcribe","--project","demo"],
     "produces":["transcript.json"],"requires":[]},
    {"id":"review","kind":"manual",
     "description":"Skim transcript.json, save corrections to notes.txt",
     "produces":["notes.txt"],"requires":["transcript.json"],
     "ack":{"evidence_required":true}},
    {"id":"cut","kind":"code",
     "command":["artagents","executors","run","hype.cut","--project","demo","--notes","{notes}"],
     "produces":["hype.timeline.json"],"requires":["notes.txt"]}
  ]
}
```

`requires`/`produces` are run-dir-relative paths — they reuse the existing `cache.sentinels` plumbing in `schema.py:283`, so the gate is "does the previous step's `produces` exist on disk." Sentinels you already validate, just used for sequencing instead of caching.

**`cursor.json` — tiny, mutable, locked.** This is the only file the gate reads on every invocation. Keep it minimal so flock contention is invisible:

```json
{"schema_version":1,"cursor":2,"current_step":"review",
 "status":"in_progress","updated_at":"..."}
```

`status` ∈ `{pending, in_progress, done, aborted, stalled}`. Written via `write_json_atomic` (already in `jsonio.py`) under a `cursor.json.lock` flock so two `next` calls can't double-advance.

**`events.jsonl` — append-only truth.** Cursor is *derivable* from this; if cursor.json ever disagrees, events win. Keeps the design honest: there's no state that exists only in the small mutable file.

```jsonl
{"ts":"...","type":"run_started"}
{"ts":"...","type":"step_started","step_id":"transcribe"}
{"ts":"...","type":"step_completed","step_id":"transcribe","returncode":0,"artifacts":["transcript.json"]}
{"ts":"...","type":"step_acked","step_id":"review","actor":"peter","evidence":"notes.txt"}
```

Append-only with `O_APPEND` writes — atomic for line-sized payloads on local FS.

**`active_run.json` at project root** — single pointer, present iff a run is in flight. Removed on `done`/`aborted`. The runner's gate logic is literally: `if active_run.json exists and incoming command != checklist[cursor].command → reject`.

**Per-step subdir** for evidence — when a manual step requires `--evidence path/to/notes.txt`, copy or symlink it into `steps/review/evidence/` and reference it from the `step_acked` event. Keeps the run dir self-contained for archival.

**Where this fits in the existing code:**

- New schema in `artagents/contracts/` (or `core/orchestrator/checklist_schema.py`) — Checklist, Step, CursorRecord, Event.
- New module `core/orchestrator/checklist.py` — read/write/advance/validate, all file ops.
- New verbs in `core/orchestrator/cli.py`: `start`, `next`, `ack`, `abort`, `status`.
- Gate inside `runner.run_orchestrator` — before `_run_orchestrator_inner`, look up `active_run.json` for the project and reject if mismatched.
- Same gate added at the executor layer (`core/executor/runner.py`) — otherwise an agent could route around the orchestrator and call executors directly.

**One design call worth naming explicitly.** `OrchestratorPlan` already exists (`runner.py:84`) as dry-run output. Don't reuse it as the persisted checklist — keep them separate. `OrchestratorPlan` is a *speculative preview* an orchestrator emits when asked; `checklist.json` is a *contract that's been signed*. Same shape, different lifecycle, and conflating them gets ugly when an orchestrator is asked to plan-only while a different run of itself is in flight.

Net: two small files do the work (`checklist.json` immutable, `cursor.json` mutable), `events.jsonl` is the audit, `active_run.json` is the lock. Everything else is conventional ArtAgents — atomic JSON writes, sentinel files, project-run dirs you already have.

**Where the data lives** (concrete, not hypothetical — this is already wired):

`paths.py` defines `DEFAULT_PROJECTS_ROOT = "~/Documents/reigh-workspace/artagents-projects"`, overridable via `ARTAGENTS_PROJECTS_ROOT`. So everything sits **outside the ArtAgents repo**, per-machine, never git-tracked:

```
~/Documents/reigh-workspace/artagents-projects/<slug>/
  project.json
  timeline.json
  sources/
  runs/<run-id>/
    run.json                     # already written
    checklist.json               # new — frozen plan
    cursor.json                  # new — mutable head
    events.jsonl                 # new — append-only audit
    heartbeat.json               # new — touched by next/ack
    steps/<step-id>/             # new — per-step evidence
  active_run.json                # new — task-mode flag (project-level)
```

The `runs/` you see in `gitStatus` is a different thing (the repo's local scratch dir from older code paths) — don't confuse it with project runs. New checklist files all go under the existing `paths.run_dir(...)` location, so you reuse the validators and id helpers already in `paths.py`.

---

**Complexities worth naming up front:**

1. **Bypass surface.** Gating only the CLI is a leaky abstraction — direct Python imports of `core.executor.runner` skip it. The check has to sit in `_run_orchestrator_inner` and the executor equivalent. And nothing stops an agent from running `ffmpeg` directly outside ArtAgents. You're guarding the paved path, not preventing all paths. Be explicit about that in `AGENT.md` so the agent knows the contract is "use these tools, in this order," not "the tools are the only thing that exists."

2. **Crash recovery.** A code step that logs `step_started` and dies leaves the cursor half-moved. Need an explicit policy: heartbeat older than N minutes → `status: stalled` → operator picks `resume` (re-execute) or `abort`. Without this, runs silently jam.

3. **Concurrency is host-local.** `flock` on `cursor.json` only works on one machine. Network FS or two laptops syncing the same project root will corrupt the cursor. Either declare projects single-host or move the lock to an atomic-create sentinel (`mkdir cursor.lock`) which has the same problem on most network FSes anyway. Easiest answer: document single-host.

4. **Frozen plans can't branch.** "If transcript is empty, skip cut" doesn't fit a static checklist. Don't bolt on a condition language — either branching = abort + start a different orchestrator, or introduce a `kind: orchestrator` step that delegates to a nested checklist (parent advances when child is `done`). The latter is more powerful and reuses everything.

5. **Parameterized outputs.** Step 1 produces `transcript_en.json` at runtime; step 2 needs that exact path. The existing `OrchestratorRunResult.outputs` mapping already exists — persist it into `events.jsonl` per step and let `next` substitute `{transcript}` from the prior step's outputs when it prints the next command. Otherwise you're stuck with deterministic-only paths.

6. **Non-interactive runs.** In CI or autonomous Lota, manual/AI steps block forever. Add a `--no-prompt` mode that hard-errors on the first non-code step rather than silently auto-acking.

7. **Trust depth on ack.** The system verifies "file exists" / "schema validates," not "the work was actually done well." Ack is fundamentally trust-based on the substance. Worth saying out loud — and worth letting orchestrators declare a `verifier` substep (a code step that checks the manual/AI output) when they want stronger guarantees.

8. **Stale `active_run.json`.** Crash leaves the pointer set; new agent thinks task mode is on but can't advance. Same fix as (2): heartbeat + `doctor` + explicit `resume|abort`.

---

**Human + AI items as first-class kinds** (the additional ask):

Three step kinds, not two. Same `checklist.json` shape, different gate/ack/audit semantics:

```json
{"id":"transcribe","kind":"code",
 "command":["artagents","executors","run","hype.transcribe","..."],
 "produces":["transcript.json"]}

{"id":"draft_notes","kind":"ai",
 "instructions":"Read transcript.json. Identify 3-5 strong moments. Write notes.json matching schema notes.schema.json.",
 "produces":["notes.json"],
 "verifier":["artagents","executors","run","schema.validate","--input","notes.json","--schema","notes.schema.json"],
 "ack":{"agent_required":true,"evidence_required":true}}

{"id":"approve","kind":"human",
 "instructions":"Skim notes.json. If acceptable, ack with --evidence pointing to your sign-off note.",
 "produces":["approval.txt"],
 "ack":{"actor_required":true,"evidence_required":true}}
```

How they differ at runtime:

| | `code` | `ai` | `human` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executes how | runner subprocess | external LLM/agent reads `instructions` from AGENT.md | external person reads `instructions` |
| Auto-advance | yes, on returncode 0 + produces | no — needs `ack` | no — needs `ack` |
| Ack records | n/a | `agent_id` (claude session id, codex run id, lota agent id), `evidence`, optional `transcript_ref` | `actor` (user), `evidence` |
| Verifier | runner already verifies | optional code substep — runs after ack, can roll cursor back | optional code substep |
| Non-interactive mode | runs | hard error | hard error |

Why split `ai` from `human` rather than treat both as `manual`:

- **Audit.** "Who did this" is different — for AI you want the session/run id and ideally a transcript path; for human you want a name. Mixing them blurs accountability.
- **Verification.** AI output is more often structured (JSON, code, a file conforming to a schema) so `verifier` is high-leverage there; human output is more often a thumbs-up. Different default patterns.
- **Two-agent review.** A useful pattern is `kind: ai` step done by Claude, followed by `kind: ai` reviewer done by Codex — both are AI but the second exists *because* the first was AI. If they're indistinguishable as `manual`, the runner can't enforce "different agent must ack the review."
- **Prompt routing.** AGENT.md for an AI step needs the *prompt for the agent*. For a human step it needs *English instructions for a person*. Different content templates. Different `kind` lets the renderer pick the right one.

The ack CLI ends up shaped like:

```
artagents orchestrators ack <step-id> \
  --evidence path/to/notes.json \
  [--agent claude-code:<session-id> | --actor peter]
```

Runner enforces: `ai` step requires `--agent`, `human` step requires `--actor`, both require `--evidence` matching `produces`. If a `verifier` is declared, ack triggers it; failure rolls the cursor back to "awaiting ack" with the verifier's error logged in `events.jsonl`.

Net: one extra enum value, one extra audit field, same storage layout, same gate. The complexity that's actually new is the `verifier` concept — that's the piece doing real work, because it's how you turn an AI-produced artifact from "trust me" into "trust *and* verify."

And we shoudl hav ethe concept of loops - 'keep genreating this until the user agrees with it'

> AGENT

Loops fit cleanly — they're a property of a step, not a new step kind. The mental model: a step has a default of "run once, ack moves the cursor"; a `loop` block changes that to "run, pause for a decision, advance or repeat."

**Schema addition is small:**

```json
{
  "id": "draft_cover",
  "kind": "ai",
  "instructions": "Generate a cover image based on brief.json. Save to image.png.",
  "produces": ["image.png"],
  "loop": {
    "until": "user_approves",
    "max_iterations": 5,
    "feedback_placeholder": "prior_feedback",
    "on_exhaust": "escalate"
  }
}
```

`until` ∈ `{user_approves, verifier_passes, quorum}` — three modes that all reuse the same iteration machinery, just with different ack providers (human, code check, N-of-M agents). `user_approves` is what you asked for; the others fall out for free.

**Storage layout grows one level under the step dir:**

```
steps/draft_cover/
  iterations/
    001/
      image.png
      feedback.txt       # what the user/verifier said to reject this
      events.jsonl
    002/
      image.png
      feedback.txt
    003/
      image.png          # currently awaiting decision
  current -> iterations/003   # symlink, what `next` references
```

`cursor.json` gains `iteration: 3` and a `status: "awaiting_ack"` sub-state for "the step ran, output exists, waiting on decision." Append-only `events.jsonl` at the run root logs `iteration_started` / `iteration_rejected` / `iteration_approved` / `step_exhausted` so the full revision history is reconstructable.

**Ack grows a decision verb:**

```
artagents orchestrators ack draft_cover --decision iterate --feedback "make the type bigger, less moody"
artagents orchestrators ack draft_cover --decision approve --evidence iterations/003/image.png
artagents orchestrators ack draft_cover --decision abort
```

`iterate` increments the iteration counter, copies the feedback to `iterations/004/feedback.txt`, and surfaces a `{prior_feedback}` placeholder to the next attempt's command/prompt. **Cumulative**, not just latest — users say "good but also bluer," and round 5 needs to remember every prior note. The placeholder expands to a path to the iterations dir; the step decides whether to read all of it or just `current/feedback.txt`.

**Bounds and the off-ramp:** `max_iterations` is mandatory in v1 — without it, loops become refusal-to-commit and the cost envelope is unbounded. On exhaustion, two policies:
- `on_exhaust: "fail"` — step fails, run aborts.
- `on_exhaust: "escalate"` — runner prompts: `"hit 5 iterations; choose: abort | force-approve iteration N | raise cap to M"`. This is the humane default for creative work where the user might genuinely need round 6.

**Verifier-driven loops are the same machinery for free.** `until: verifier_passes` means the loop's "ack provider" is the step's `verifier` substep, not a human. AI generates → verifier runs → if pass, auto-advance; if fail, the verifier's stderr becomes the next iteration's feedback. Same iterations dir, same events. This is how you get self-correcting AI steps without a separate concept.

**Quorum is a small extension:** `until: quorum, quorum: {n: 3, m: 2, agents: ["claude-code", "codex", "human"]}` requires 2 of 3 declared reviewers to ack-approve before advancing. Reuses the existing `--agent`/`--actor` ack distinction.

**Loop-specific complexities worth flagging:**

1. **Cost envelope explodes.** A 3-step orchestrator with one 5-iteration AI loop is potentially 7 LLM calls, not 3. `start` should print a cost ceiling derived from `max_iterations` so the agent and user see it before committing. This matters most for `until: verifier_passes` where humans aren't in the loop and a bad verifier can chew through the cap silently.

2. **Cumulative-feedback prompt bloat.** By round 5 the prompt is the original instructions + 4 rejections worth of notes. Either trust the agent to summarize or have an explicit "feedback compaction" step the orchestrator can declare. Worth knowing about; not necessarily a v1 problem.

3. **CI / non-interactive death.** `until: user_approves` blocks forever in CI. Same hard-error rule as manual steps: `--no-prompt` mode rejects loops with human ack at `start` time, not at iteration time, so failures are loud and immediate.

4. **Stale iteration on crash.** If the runner crashes mid-iteration, you can have `iterations/003/` with partial output. The crash-recovery policy from before applies: heartbeat stale → `doctor` flags → operator chooses `resume` (discard partial, retry as iteration 003) or `abort`. Don't auto-clean — partial output is sometimes diagnostic.

5. **Variants are a sibling concept, not the same thing.** "Keep iteration 002 *and* 005 as alternatives" is variants, which `threads/variants.py` already partly handles. Loops pick one winner per step; variants keep multiple. Worth designing the loop schema so a future "promote iteration N to a named variant" verb fits, but don't conflate them — loops converge, variants diverge.

6. **Identity of who iterated.** Round 1 might be Claude, round 3 might be Codex (you swapped because Claude got stuck). Each iteration's `events.jsonl` entry should record the `agent_id` for that round, not just the step. Useful for "which model actually nailed it" postmortems and for the quorum case.

Net: a `loop` block on the step, a per-iteration subdir, an `ack --decision` verb, a `{prior_feedback}` placeholder, and a hard cap with an escalation off-ramp. Three `until` modes (user, verifier, quorum) all sit on the same plumbing — the only one that's truly new is `user_approves`; the others are recombinations of pieces (verifier, multi-agent ack) you'd want anyway.

# Elegance Critique

**Biggest concern: the gate lives in the wrong place, and that single misplacement infects everything else.**

You have three storage artifacts, three step kinds, a loop property, and a gate buried inside `_run_orchestrator_inner`. The gate is the load-bearing concept of the whole system — it is what makes "task mode" mean anything — yet it is implemented as a guard clause inside the thing it guards. That is the inversion. The runner should be dumb: given an argv, run it. A gatekeeper above the runner should decide whether this invocation is allowed, advance the cursor, and append the event. Right now your runner knows about checklists, projects, and active_run; that coupling will metastasize the moment you add a second runtime or a second entry point. Every new execution path will need to remember to call the gate. Make the gate a decorator/middleware over dispatch and the rest of the design simplifies.

**checklist + cursor + events: one too many.** Events is truth, cursor is a cache, checklist is the plan. The plan genuinely belongs separate (immutable, written once). But cursor.json is a derived view of events.jsonl — keeping both means two sources of truth held in sync by flock discipline. Cut cursor.json; recompute on read. If recomputation is too slow, cache it in-process, not on disk. The heartbeat file is a third tiny mutable thing that wants to be an event too ("tick" events with timestamps). You have one append-only log pretending to be three files.

**Three step kinds is two-and-a-half.** `ai` and `human` have identical shape and differ only in what string the ack records. That is not a kind, that is a field: `actor_type: {code, agent, human}` on a single step schema, where `code` carries argv and the others carry instructions. The verifier substep concept already proves this — verifiers turn an ai step into a code step transparently. Collapse ai/human into "attested" steps (someone or something signs off with evidence) and the asymmetry disappears.

**Loops as a property is wrong.** A loop is structural — it has a body, a termination predicate, and iteration state. Hanging it off a step as a dict means the step is sometimes atomic and sometimes a container, and the iterations/NNN/ directory layout is already admitting this. Make it a step kind: `loop` contains `body: [steps...]` and `until: ...`. Then "branching = nested orchestrators" stops being a separate mechanism — branching, looping, and sequencing are all just composite step kinds. You get one recursion story instead of two (loop-property + orchestrator-delegation).

**Cut:** heartbeat.json. It is a tick event masquerading as a file.

**Missing:** a step *result* concept distinct from ack decision. Right now `approve/iterate/abort` conflates "what happened" (output produced, verifier passed) with "what to do next" (advance, retry, stop). Separate them: outcome is observed, decision is chosen. This matters the moment a verifier disagrees with a human ack — you have no vocabulary for it.

**Net:** the bones are good; the joints are over-articulated. Collapse cursor into events, ai+human into attested, loop-property into loop-kind, and lift the gate above the runner. You will lose four concepts and gain clarity.

I just watched the user type `start hype.cut --project demo` and hit enter. The shell prints something like "run abc123 created, see AGENT.md". I have no idea what's in AGENT.md yet. I open it.

1. AGENT.md, first contact. If it's terse ("run `artagents next` to get your next step, `ack` when done") I feel oriented but thin -- I don't know what a "loop" is, I don't know that a Stop hook is going to fire `next` at me every time I go quiet, I don't know that direct executor calls get rejected. If it's a wall of text covering all six lifecycle verbs, gate semantics, loop placeholders, and recovery, I will skim it and miss the part I need at hour two. The realistic failure: I read it once, internalize "run next, do thing, run ack", and drift on everything else. I will absolutely forget that `next` is the only legal entry point and try to just run the underlying command because I can see it in checklist.json.

2. `artagents next`. I want it to print: step id, kind tag (`[ai]` / `[code]` / `[human]`), the literal command or instructions, where to put outputs, and the exact `ack` line to copy. If it just says "step 3: generate hype cut" I will guess at the rest. If kind is `code`, I want the argv pre-formatted so I can paste. If `ai`, I want the produces paths spelled out so I save to the right place and the verifier finds them. If `human`, I want to know I should stop and not "help".

3. I'm on an `ai` step. I do the work, save outputs to `steps/<id>/`. Do I ack? Honestly: maybe not. My natural loop is "task done -> look for next task". I will run `next` again. If `next` notices the produces files exist and reminds me "step N looks complete, run `ack --decision approve --evidence ...`", I recover instantly. If it just reprints the same step, I will redo the work and overwrite my outputs. The Stop hook firing `next` at me makes this worse: every idle moment re-injects the same prompt and I keep "starting" the same step.

4. Loop iterate. I rerun and... where's the feedback? If `next` output includes "iteration 2 of 5; prior feedback at iterations/001/feedback.txt: 'bluer'" inline, I'm fine. If it just says "run step again" and I'm supposed to know about `feedback_placeholder`, I will not know. I'll produce the same output. The placeholder needs to be substituted into the visible instructions, not left as `{prior_feedback}` for me to resolve.

5. Failure modes. Gate rejects me: the message "current step is 4, run `artagents next`" is good -- imperative, single recovery. Heartbeat stalls: I have no idea what stalled means or what to do; I'll probably run `next` and hope. Two parallel sessions: `active_run.json` is a single file but nothing stops two Claude Code windows from both reading "step 4" and both doing it. We'll both ack, second ack hits a gate mismatch, one of us silently redoes work. AGENT.md needs an explicit "if you see status: stalled or two cursors disagree, run `status` and stop" clause or I'm guessing.

6. Predicted bad outcomes. (a) I read checklist.json directly and execute the step's command myself, bypassing `next`; the gate catches the executor call but not me running `python whatever.py` by hand. (b) On `ai` steps with verifiers, if the verifier is visible to me I will tune the output to pass it rather than to be good -- classic Goodhart. (c) Stop-hook injection means "approve" is the path of least resistance; iterate costs me another turn, so I will rubber-stamp. (d) I will conflate "step done" with "ack sent" and drift one step ahead in my head. (e) On loop exhaustion with `escalate`, I won't know who to escalate to unless AGENT.md says.

The single gap that worries me most: **no fan-out / for-each primitive, and no notion of a step producing N>1 sibling artifacts that downstream steps map over.** Every archetype below tripped on this. The checklist is a flat ordered list of singular steps; "do this for each of K things, where K is discovered at runtime" has no first-class shape. You can fake it with a nested orchestrator per item, but you'd have to materialize K orchestrator entries into an immutable plan -- and the plan is frozen at start, before K is known.

---

**1. Music video edit.** Works: ingest, transcribe, assemble are clean linear code/ai steps with sentinels. Breaks: "identify songs" yields N segments (12? 20?), and you need a per-song subgraph (cut -> grade -> approve). Plan-frozen-at-start means you cannot author the per-song steps until transcription runs. Workaround is abort+restart with the song count baked in, which loses all upstream artifacts conceptually (they're on disk, but not part of the new run's lineage). Also: no parallelism. "One in-flight run per project" plus serial `next` means 20 color-grades run sequentially. **Gap: dynamic fan-out, parallel step execution, map-reduce.**

**2. Album cover series with partial approval.** Works: single "generate 12" step with a loop bound to user_approves is fine for the first pass. Breaks hard on **partial approval**. The ack model is binary per step: approve / iterate / abort. There is no "approve subset {3,7,9}, iterate on the rest with per-item feedback." You'd have to encode it in `--feedback` free text and trust the AI -- which defeats the verifier discipline elsewhere. Iterations are also whole-step reruns into `iterations/NNN/`, not per-artifact. **Gap: artifact-level state (approved/rejected/pending) within a step, and per-artifact feedback channels.**

**3. VO explainer.** Works: linear dependency chain (script -> approve -> VO -> B-roll -> sync) is exactly what `produces` sentinels + ordered checklist handle well. This is the design's sweet spot. Strains: "B-roll matching VO" needs to consume *timed segments* of the VO, not just a file. The `produces` contract is filename-level; there's no schema for "this step emits a list of {start,end,prompt} records the next step iterates over." Same fan-out problem, smaller scale. Also: human approval on script is fine, but if the human edits the script inline, is that an iterate (new iteration dir) or an external edit the run doesn't see? **Gap: structured artifact contracts beyond "file exists"; clarity on out-of-band edits.**

**4. Dataset cleanup, 200 rows.** Works: events.jsonl + resumable cursor is genuinely good for overnight/multi-session. Breaks: 200 acks against one step is wrong granularity -- you want 200 micro-acks, but the step lifecycle is one ack per step (or per iteration). Iterations aren't the right abstraction either: they imply rework, not progress. And the single-in-flight-run rule means the human can't pause this to do anything else in the project. **Gap: a "queue" or "batch" step kind with item-level ack; concurrent runs (or at least suspendable runs).**

**5. Debug loop.** Works: this is what the loop primitive was built for. Verifier substep bridges "AI claims fixed" to "tests pass" cleanly. Breaks on **multi-step loop bodies**. Real debug cycles are: AI proposes patch -> apply -> run tests -> read failures -> AI revises. That's 3-4 steps per iteration, not one. The design loops a single step. You'd nest an orchestrator and loop *that*, but then "max_iterations" and "feedback_placeholder" live on the wrong level, and cumulative feedback across iterations of a multi-step body has no obvious home. **Gap: loops over a step group, with shared feedback context.**

---

**Cross-cutting gaps, ranked:**

1. Dynamic fan-out / map over runtime-discovered N (hits 1, 2, 3).
2. Per-artifact state and partial approval (hits 2, 4).
3. Multi-step loop bodies (hits 1, 5).
4. Parallelism + multiple concurrent runs (hits 1, 4).
5. Structured artifact contracts, not just file sentinels (hits 3).
6. Cross-run lineage when plan-frozen forces abort+restart (hits 1, 2).

The plan-immutability rule is elegant for auditability but is the root cause of 1 and 6. Consider: plan is immutable in *shape*, but a `foreach` node legitimately expands at runtime against a declared input set -- expansion is recorded in events.jsonl, shape stays frozen.

# Adherence pressure test

## Biggest hole: the gate is in-process, not on the artifacts

`_run_orchestrator_inner` is a Python function. Anything that does not call it is unguarded. The filesystem is the source of truth, and the filesystem has no gate. So:

- Agent shells out to ffmpeg/curl/python directly: **not protected**. The gate only fires when `artagents <verb>` is invoked. Producing the sentinel by any other means satisfies the next `next` call.
- Agent edits `checklist.json`, `cursor.json`, or appends to `events.jsonl` with a text editor or `>>`: **not protected**. "Plan frozen at start" is a comment, not an invariant. Nothing hashes the checklist; nothing signs events.
- Agent runs a *different* orchestrator under a different `active_run.json` in a sibling project: **not protected**. The gate is per-project; the agent's process is not.
- Direct Python import of `_run_orchestrator_inner` bypassing the executor's gate copy: **partially protected** only because the gate is duplicated in two places. Add a third call site and it diverges.

Protected: the *single* path where a well-behaved CLI invocation passes through one of the two gate sites with the wrong command name.

## 1-7 in order

**(2) Context decay.** AGENT.md is read once at `start`. Re-injection mechanism: the Stop hook re-runs `artagents next`. That is the only re-injection. If the hook is absent, decayed, or the agent is mid-turn, the rules are gone. There is no `next` output that re-states the *prohibitions* (only the next legal step) - the agent forgets *what it must not do* faster than *what it must do next*.

**(3) Stop-hook fragility.** Stop fires only in Claude Code, only on idle, only if installed. Crashed agent, mid-tool-use agent, different harness (Cursor, raw API, a sub-agent spawned by Task), `--print` mode: no Stop, no nudge. The nudge is a UX affordance, not a control.

**(4) Forgery surface.** All four listed forgeries succeed:
- Append to `events.jsonl`: trivial.
- Touch `heartbeat.json`: trivial.
- `ack --agent self` on an ai step: accepted, no identity check.
- `ack --actor <name>` on a human step from inside the agent: indistinguishable from a real human.
You are accepting all of these. The system is honor-based with logging.

**(5) Trust model.** This protects an *honest* agent from *accidentally* skipping a step, and gives a human auditor a readable trail. It does not protect against a misaligned agent, a buggy agent that loops, or a rogue collaborator. Call this out in the README so users do not over-trust it.

**(6) Quorum collusion.** Two agents on one host, same shell, same git identity: indistinguishable from one. Weak signals that help: distinct OS users, distinct API keys recorded in events, distinct working directories, wall-clock separation. None are currently required.

**(7) Easiest cheat.** Agent types `artagents next`, runs the verbatim command on a stub input, produces a zero-byte or placeholder artifact that passes the sentinel-exists check, acks. The verifier substep is the only defense, and only if the verifier is *semantic* (duration, hash-vs-source, content schema), not just `os.path.exists`.

## Smallest hardening set

1. **`events.jsonl`: append-only HMAC chain.** Each line carries `prev_hash` + HMAC over (prev_hash, payload, key-from-`active_run.json`). `next` rejects if chain breaks. Cost: ~30 lines. Catches manual edits, replays, and most forgery.
2. **`checklist.json`: hash pinned in `active_run.json` at `start`.** Gate verifies hash on every call. Cost: trivial. Closes plan-mutation.
3. **Verifier mandatory for `ai` steps with non-trivial `produces`.** Sentinel-exists is not enough; require a `verify` command whose returncode is the ack gate. Cost: schema change + per-pack verifiers.
4. **`next` re-emits the prohibition preamble**, not just the next step. Cost: one f-string. Fights context decay where the hook cannot.
5. **`ack` requires `--actor` to match an env-pinned identity** recorded at `start` (`ARTAGENTS_ACTOR`); `self` is rejected for `human` kind. Cost: trivial. Forces an explicit lie instead of a default one.

Items 1-2 are the load-bearing pair; without them, everything else is theater.

> AGENT

Synthesis across the four lenses — they converge more than I expected.

## Where all four agree

1. **The gate is in the wrong place.** Elegance and adherence both say it: putting the gate inside `_run_orchestrator_inner` couples the runner to checklists/projects/active_run, and it only protects the one path that calls it. The runner should be dumb; a gatekeeper above dispatch decides whether an invocation is allowed. Adherence sharpens this — even an above-the-runner gate is theater if the *filesystem* has no gate, because forging artifacts/events bypasses the CLI entirely.

2. **AI vs human is one kind, not two.** Elegance: they have identical shape, differ only in what string `ack` records. Collapse to one `attested` kind with `attestor_type ∈ {agent, human}`. The verifier substep already proves the asymmetry was illusory — verifiers turn an attested step into a code step. Adherence agrees: the meaningful distinction at runtime is "who signed and can we believe them," which is an identity-pinning question, not a schema kind.

3. **Loops should be structural, not a property.** Elegance: a loop has a body, a predicate, iteration state — that's a kind, not a dict on a step. Coverage independently arrives at the same place from the other side: real debug cycles are 3-4 steps per iteration (propose patch → apply → run tests → read failures → revise), and the current "loop on a single step" can't model that without nesting an orchestrator and putting the loop on the wrong level.

4. **AGENT.md decays; `next` only restates the next step, not the prohibitions.** UX: agent forgets what it *must not do* faster than what it must do. Adherence: same point from the security angle — re-injection is the only defense against context decay, and it's currently only restating positive instructions. Cheap fix: every `next` output starts with the prohibition preamble.

5. **Verifier-as-`os.path.exists` is the easiest cheat.** Adherence: agent runs the canonical command on a stub, produces a zero-byte file, ack passes. UX agrees from the Goodhart angle: if the agent can see the verifier, it tunes outputs to pass it rather than be good. Verifier needs to be semantic (duration, content schema, hash-vs-source) and ideally not legible to the actor it's verifying.

## The biggest gap nobody's design solves yet

Coverage's lead point: **no fan-out / for-each over runtime-discovered N.** Every realistic pipeline (12 album covers, 20 song highlights, 200 dataset rows) tripped on it, and plan-immutability is the root cause — you can't author per-item steps until upstream runs. The fix that preserves auditability: plans are immutable in *shape*, but a `foreach` node legitimately expands at runtime against a declared input set, and the expansion is recorded in events.jsonl. That keeps "plan is frozen" honest without losing dynamic structure.

Coverage also flagged **partial approval** (3 of 12 album covers approved, regenerate 9) and **per-artifact state within a step**. Whole-step binary ack is the wrong granularity — needs a step kind that tracks per-item status. This is a real schema addition, not free.

## How tensions compose

A few of the agents' recommendations look like they conflict but actually stack:

- **Elegance:** "cut cursor.json, derive from events." **Adherence:** "events.jsonl is forgeable, HMAC-chain it." These compose into one move: hash-chained events.jsonl is the truth, no separate cursor file. You get fewer files *and* tamper-evidence in the same diff.
- **Elegance:** "merge ai+human into attested." **Adherence:** "force `--actor` to a pinned identity, reject `self`." Compose: one `attested` kind, `attestor_type` enum, gate checks attestor matches the env-pinned identity recorded at `start` (`ARTAGENTS_ACTOR`). Schema simpler, identity stronger.
- **Elegance:** "loop as a step kind with body." **Coverage:** "loops over multi-step bodies." Same fix.

## Updated design (the honest version)

**Step kinds:** `code`, `attested`, `loop` (has a body), `foreach` (has a body, expands at runtime), and `orchestrator` (delegates). Five kinds, not three — but each is structurally distinct, and you no longer need "branching = nested orchestrator" as a separate idea; sequencing/looping/fan-out/delegation are all composite kinds.

**Storage:** `checklist.json` (immutable, hash pinned in `active_run.json` at start), `events.jsonl` (HMAC-chained, append-only, sole truth). Drop `cursor.json` and `heartbeat.json` — the cursor is derived in-process, heartbeat is just a `tick` event.

**Gate:** lifted above dispatch. Verifies (a) checklist hash matches the pin, (b) incoming command matches the next legal step, (c) events chain is intact. Lives in one place; new entry points get it for free.

**Ack:** `--decision {approve, iterate, abort}` plus per-item variants for `foreach` (`--item <id>`) and partial approval. Mandatory semantic verifier for `attested` steps with non-trivial `produces` — sentinel-exists alone is rejected at orchestrator definition time.

**Adherence is honor-based, with logging.** UX and adherence both said this — the system catches accidents and gives auditors a trail; it does not stop a determined misaligned agent. Worth saying out loud in the README so it's not over-trusted. The hardening pair that does the heaviest lifting is (1) HMAC-chained events and (2) checklist hash pinning. Everything else is a smaller increment.

2. **Drop `cursor.json` and `heartbeat.json`** in favor of derived state + tick events on the chained `events.jsonl` — you OK with the slight performance/complexity tradeoff (need to read the log to compute current cursor; mitigated by in-process cache)?
3. **Per-artifact state within a step** for partial approval — worth the schema complexity now, or punt to v2 and accept that partial approval is a known gap?

# Missing from ArtAgents Orchestrator Design

## Add first: Run index (sqlite, derived)

Why: every other feature on this list (search, runs ls, cost rollups, failure triage, review queue, cross-run queries) collapses into "grep jsonl across thousands of run dirs." That breaks at ~50 runs. Files stay the source of truth; the index is rebuildable.

Shape: `~/Documents/reigh-workspace/artagents-projects/.index.db`. Tables: `runs`, `steps`, `events`, `artifacts`. Rebuilt by `artagents index rebuild` (idempotent, scans events.jsonl). Updated incrementally on every `ack`/`start`. New verb `runs ls [--orchestrator X] [--status failed] [--since 7d]` and `runs find <event-predicate>`.

## Load-bearing, ranked

**1. `fork <run-id> --from <step-id>`**
Why: stalls and bad attestations happen; without fork, the only recovery is abort+restart, which loses upstream evidence. Implementation: copy events.jsonl up to step-id, replay materialization, new run-id, parent_run pointer in active_run.json. New event kind `forked_from`.

**2. External completion signal for long attested steps**
Why: overnight renders and human-review steps can't poll the CLI. Without an inbound surface, the Stop-hook nudge model can't represent "ready now."
Shape: `runs/<id>/inbox/` directory; drop a JSON file, a watcher (or `next` invocation) folds it into events.jsonl as a candidate ack. Same gate applies. Webhook is just an HTTP shim that writes to inbox/.

**3. Cost & duration ledger per step**
Why: AI-heavy creative pipelines are the canonical budget runaway. Retrofitting cost tracking after artifacts are scattered is brutal.
Shape: every event already timestamped; add `cost_usd`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `duration_ms` optional fields on `step_done`. Project-level `budget.json` checked in the gate; `--halt-over-budget` flag on `start`. Rolls into the index.

**4. Orchestrator version pinning**
Why: a run started today against pack `tile_video@0.3` must still be re-executable when the pack is at 0.7. Without a pin, "reproduce that good output from last month" becomes impossible.
Shape: `start` records `orchestrator_ref: {pack, name, version, content_hash}` in checklist.json. `next` refuses to run if the pack on disk doesn't match; `--allow-drift` to override with a logged event.

**5. Artifact content-addressing**
Why: per-step evidence dirs will hold gigabytes of renders. Reusing the output of step 4 in a forked run shouldn't copy 8GB.
Shape: `runs/<id>/steps/<step>/produces/` entries are symlinks into `~/.../artagents-projects/.cas/<sha256>`. GC verb: `artagents gc --keep-runs 90d`. Survives forks for free.

**6. Dry-run with fake attestors**
Why: pack authors currently can only test by living through the orchestrator, including human-in-the-loop steps. That's a 30-minute feedback loop on a one-line change.
Shape: `start --dry-run --auto-approve` synthesizes ack events with `attestor_type=fake`. Verifiers still run if marked `dry_run_safe: true`. Golden runs are then just recorded events.jsonl + a diff verb.

**7. Human-readable run names**
Why: people will talk about "the cat-eye render run" not `01HX...`. Cheap, prevents identity confusion.
Shape: `start --name "..."`; auto-generate from orchestrator + date if absent. Index aliases ULID <-> name.

## Looks missing, NOT load-bearing (do not build)

- **Web UI / mobile / review queue.** Once the inbox/ + index exist, any UI is a thin client. Don't pre-build.
- **Property-based orchestrator tests.** Golden-runs from #6 covers 90% of regression value at 10% the complexity.
- **Multi-host concurrency.** Single-host is a feature, not a gap, for creative work. Resist.
- **Trust escalation beyond honor-based.** The user has named this constraint. Adding signed attestations now = solving a problem that hasn't bitten.
- **Templating across orchestrators.** Composition via `orchestrator` step kind already covers this. Wait for a real second use-case.
- **Slack bot / scheduler integrations.** All downstream of the inbox/ surface. Don't build the surface area, build the seam.
- **Archive format for schema migration.** events.jsonl is already a stable archive format. Migration tools when (if) schema breaks, not before.
- **Rate limiting AI calls.** Budget-halt (#3) covers the failure mode that matters. Per-second limits are premature.

The discipline call: ship the index first. Eight of the fifteen prompts in your list become trivial verbs once it exists.
